transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martin (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Rajiv Patel (Stellar Data - Dir ML), Maya Chen (Stellar Infra), Liam O'Connor (Stellar Security)

--- Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect) ---
Priya: quick sync, focus on network retries and upgrade path for the private pilot.
Alex: grave of notes, pricing and next steps.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alex: All right, thanks everyone for joining. Um let's do quick roll call - Priya and I from Redwood, and from Stellar Rajiv, Maya, Liam. Can you hear us ok?
[00:12] Rajiv: Yep, hearing you, thanks. Sorry ran a bit late x2 on my side.
[00:18] Maya: here, sorry, just hopped in.
[00:20] Liam: here as well.
[00:22] Priya: great. Agenda for today: network troubleshooting update, results from the latest runtime 1.4.2 smoke tests, and plan for the canary upgrade next week.
[00:32] Alex: quick context: last week we saw intermittent RPC timeouts between the Redwood runtime and the customer model nodes - looked like NAT translation exhaustion and some ephemeral port depletion on the Transit Gateway.
[00:46] Maya: yeah we've been seeing a spike in ephemeral ports, we have a small pool and the app opens new sockets per batch in some cases. We added short-lived keepalives but still saw retries.
[00:58] Priya: sorry interrupt - that matches what we saw in the logs: a burst of simultaneous connections when you hit the long-context endpoints, the KV cache warms and causes parallel loads. Some of that could be mitigated by connection pooling in the sidecar.
[01:15] Rajiv: sidecar pooling, ok, can you point to any config we should change in k8s?
[01:19] Priya: yes, we're going to share a patch for the helm chart - reduce max connections per pod and enable HTTP/2 multiplexing where possible. We'll also add guidance for the NAT gateway (increase port range or add SNAT per instance).
[01:32] Maya: sounds good. Also side question: the 1.4.2 runtime update - did that include the faster attention kernel you mentioned? I saw notes about quantization compat.
[01:41] Alex: yeah 1.4.2 includes kernel fixes and a quantization path for int8 which improved memory footprint. We also tuned the KV cache eviction to be less aggressive so prefix reuse is higher.
[01:51] Rajiv: after the tune last night, our baseline p99 dropped from 720ms to about 510ms on short contexts, but long contexts still show 1.1s spikes.
[02:03] Priya: right - the long-tail is because of both cache misses and the current batching policy causing head-of-line blocking for single large requests. We can enable a small dedicated fast lane for low-latency single-token requests.
[02:18] Liam: from security perspective, we need to confirm KMS integration for keys used by the private control plane. Also audit logs need to be forwarded to our SIEM.
[02:28] Alex: absolutely - we have a KMS integration guide. We'll share the SOC 2 artifacts and the Private deployment checklist link: https://redwood.internal/docs/private-deploy-kms (note: internal link).
[02:40] Liam: perfect, I'll review and confirm.
[02:44] Maya: back to networking: on Tuesday we saw a complete failure of three pods during the load test, k8s evicted them, logs show OOM events and also a Node-level kernel message about conntrack table full.
[02:58] Priya: conntrack full - ok that explains the NAT errors. Workarounds: increase conntrack max, or reduce ephemeral sockets per request via pooling. We can also recommend creating a NAT gateway per availability zone to spread the SNAT mappings.
[03:12] Rajiv: if we add NAT gateways per AZ, that's going to bump cost. Any rough cost tradeoffs?
[03:17] Alex: yes, cost up for NAT gateway but improves stability. As an alternative we can propose Dedicated mode where Redwood manages GPUs in our VPC and you get predictable throughput - that's a different commercial option but lowers your per-request network overhead. We'll follow up with pricing.
[03:32] Rajiv: good to see numbers please.
[03:35] Priya: on the perf front, we ran a synthetic with 32k tokens context and the int8 path saved about 30% memory which allowed two more concurrent workers per GPU. Throughput improved about 18% for batch workloads.
[03:49] Rajiv: nice, did that affect quality? Any regression in perplexity or outputs?
[03:54] Priya: small differences on a subset of tokens; we measured with our eval harness and saw minor delta under threshold. We'll attach the evaluation CSV to the pilot channel.
[04:05] Maya: also we hit an issue with the egress firewall rules - some of the Redwood control-plane callbacks couldn't reach the customer callback endpoint because only specific ports were allowed.
[04:15] Alex: that's the callback webhook for health pings and metrics, right? We can make that optional or route via a private peering link. If you prefer no public egress, we can do VPC peering or private link.
[04:27] Liam: VPC peering sounds preferable for security, but need to see the route table changes.
[04:31] Priya: we'll provide the route table diff and an example peering template.
[04:36] Rajiv: great. On upgrade schedule, are we still targeting canary next Wednesday?
[04:42] Alex: yes tentatively Wed 2026-03-31. Plan: 10% of pods, monitor latency and error rate for 30 minutes, then 50%, then 100% if green. If we see conntrack/ephemeral errors we'll pause.
[04:55] Maya: can we add an automatic rollback threshold? Like >1% errors or >200ms p99 increase triggers rollback?
[05:03] Priya: absolutely - we'll add a canary policy: error rate threshold 0.8% and p99 increase 25% as a safety rollback. We'll share the rollout policy in the dashboard.
[05:16] Rajiv: another item - the model cache persisted between restarts? We had one restart and saw cold-start penalty of ~900ms.
[05:24] Priya: model cache persist depends on local SSD config. In the Private deploy we recommend ephemeral-ssd with pre-warming; we can add pre-warm hooks to the helm chart. That should reduce cold starts.
[05:35] Alex: also note we support persistent volume claim options if you want full persistence across restarts; depends on your storage cost tolerance.
[05:44] Liam: on compliance, can you confirm we can sign an addendum for data residency?
[05:49] Alex: yes, for Private deployments we can sign data residency addendum and you can control retention in the console. We'll send template with the SOC2/ISO attachments.
[05:58] Rajiv: quick note, last week's benchmark spreadsheet link - I shared a csv in the pilot channel (ref: drive link). Priya can you confirm you got it?
[06:05] Priya: I have it, thanks. We'll add the new 1.4.2 results to that sheet once we finish today's perf run.
[06:14] Maya: ok, any other network mitigation ideas? We considered using a proxy layer to multiplex connections.
[06:20] Priya: proxy layer could help. We recommend using an envoy sidecar with HTTP/2 to multiplex and reduce sockets. We'll include an example envoy config in the guide.
[06:31] Rajiv: perfect.
[06:33] Alex: let's go through concrete next steps and owners - quick recap.
[06:37] Priya: action: push helm patch, envoy example, route table template, and rollout policy doc by Friday (2026-03-27).
[06:46] Maya: action: collect VPC flow logs, traceroute outputs, and k8s event logs and put them in the pilot channel by Monday (2026-03-28).
[06:55] Alex: action: send Dedicated pricing and contract template by Thursday (2026-03-26).
[07:02] Liam: I'll review KMS and audit forwarding and come back with a short list of questions.
[07:08] Rajiv: timeline for the canary again?
[07:11] Alex: aiming Wed 2026-03-31, small window early UTC hours, we'll confirm after we get the flow logs and helm patch applied.
[07:19] Priya: one last technical note - we saw a rare serialization error in the trace logs that looked like a minor protobuf mismatch on control-plane health payloads, probably a version skew between agent and control plane. We'll include a compat check in the upgrade pre-check script.
[07:34] Rajiv: good catch.
[07:36] Maya: ok we're aligned. Thanks everyone.
[07:39] Alex: thanks all - we'll post notes and follow up in the pilot channel.
